newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Sept M2 supply rises 17.5 pct yr-on-yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Sept M2 supply rises 17.5 pct yr-on-yr.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose a year-on-year 17.5 percent in September against a 13.9 percent rise a year earlier, provisional figures released by the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Wednesday.
Note - M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. The BOK has stopped providing M2 figures in won.

A BOK statement said corporate money demand was rising due to a slowdown in exports and a rise in inventory. Heavy spending around the Chusok holiday, one of the most important traditional celebrations in South Korea, also contributed to increasing M2 figures in September.

The statement said M2 rose 17.3 percent year-on-year during the third quarter of this year against a 15.2 percent rise in the second quarter. Increasing corporate operation expenses and the maturity extension for trust accounts at banks caused the third quarter money supply rise.
Private sector credit rose to 18.18 trillion won during the July to September period against 6.72 trillion won a year earlier. Bank loans usually peak ahead of the holidays.

The government soaked up 2.7 trillion won against 2.44 trillion a year ago. A total of 11.75 trillion was digested by the government in the nine months of the year, compared with 9.5 trillion won during the same period of last year.

Because of a mounting deficit in the nation's current account deficit and reducing short-term trade credit, a net 5.48 trillion won was absorbed in the overseas sector, against a net inflow of 2.5 trillion a year earlier.

South Korea's current account deficit for the first eight months of the year soared to $15.24 billion, more than double the central bank's original projection of a $7 billion shortfall for the whole year.
The BOK statement said the central bank would show a flexible monetary policy in consideration of interest rates and foreign exchange rates.
The bank planned to stabilise M2 growth at around 16 percent, where it was when the bank changed regulations on trust account operations.
